Amount In The Tribunal.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This Day,

K.S.Mudagal J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
"Whether the compensation awarded to the claimants under the impugned award is just?" is the question involved in this case.
2. Respondents were claimants No.1 to 5 and appellant was the respondent in MVC 5846/2012 on the file of XXI Additional Small Causes Judge and MACT, Bengaluru.

entities.text: XXI Additional Small Causes Judge and MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. For the purpose of convenience, parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Tribunal.
Claimants 1 and 2 are the mother and father, claimants 3 to 5 are the younger sisters of deceased Kantharaju C.N.

On 16.7.2012 at 6.00 p.m. when said Kanatharaju was proceeding on Motorbike No.KA-43-K-6540 in front of Big Bazaar, West of Chord Road, Bengaluru, the bus bearing Registration No.KA-33-F-136 hit him and caused the accident.
Due to the injury suffered in the accident, he died on the spot.

5. Regarding the accident, on the complaint of one Shivakumar N., Malleswaram Traffic Police registered FIR as per Ex.P1 against the driver of the bus for the offences punishable under Sections The Managing Director vs Smt Anjenamma on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54398167/
2 279 and 304A of IPC and Sections 134(a) & (b), read with 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988.
6.

Claimants filed MVC No.5846/12 claiming that deceased was working as Lab. Assistant at Soil Science Department, GKVK, Bengaluru and in another private organization and earning Rs.11,000/-
per month.
They further contended that they were solely depending on his income and due to his death, they have suffered damages.
They claimed compensation of Rs.20,35,000/- from respondent-the owner of the bus.
The respondent contested the petition denying the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of its bus, age, occupation, income of the deceased and its liability to pay the compensation.
8. The Tribunal, on recording the evidence of the parties, at first instance on 31.05.2013 passed the award granting compensation of Rs.7,35,000/- in favour of the claimants.
The claimants and the respondent both challenged that award before this Court in MFA Nos.7775/2013 and No.2717/14(MV).

This Court, by order dated 25.2.2015, allowed those appeals and remanded the matter to the Tribunal to reconsider the issue regarding quantum of compensation after affording opportunity to both the parties to lead evidence.
9. After the matter was remanded, claimant examined PW.2.
Again respondent did not lead any evidence before the Tribunal.

The Tribunal on hearing the parties and relying on Ex.P18 the salary details held that the deceased was earning Rs.6,000/-per month from his employment in GKVK and Rs.5,000/- per month from employment with PW.2 NC: 2023:KHC:21285-DB as Supervisor of JCB.

Thus, the Tribunal assessed the total income of the deceased at Rs.11,000/- per month, added 50%
to the same by way of future prospects, deducted half of it for his personal expenses, applied `17'
multiplier and awarded compensation of Rs.16,83,000/- under the head of `loss of dependency'.
10.
The Tribunal in all awarded compensation of Rs.17,48,000/- under the different heads as per the table below.
Sl. Amount in  Heads

No. Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 16,83,000/-
 2. Loss of love & affection 20,000/-
 3. Loss of estate 25,000/-
 Transportation of dead body  4. 20,000/-
 and funeral expenses

3

11. Sri. B.L.Sanjeev, learned counsel for the appellant submits that at the time of accident, deceased was not working in GKVK, the Tribunal committed error in considering Rs.6,000/- as salary income of the deceased under the employment of GKVK.

He further submits that, respondent NC:
2023:KHC:21285-DB was not given proper opportunity to adduce its evidence.
Therefore, the respondent KSRTC has filed I.A.3/17 under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC for production of documents and for leave to adduce additional evidence.
He seeks remand of the matter for that purpose.
12. Per contra, Sri K.V.Shyamaprasada, learned counsel for the claimants submits that, despite giving sufficient opportunity, the respondent did not adduce evidence.
He further submits that the deceased was BA Graduate and had undergone Computer certification course.

He further submits,
salary certificate as per Ex.P11 and salary details as per P18 were not disputed in the cross-examination.
Therefore, Tribunal was justified in considering both the incomes.
The impugned award does not warrant any interference.
ANALYSIS 13.
It is settled position of law that when a person expects the Court to believe existence of a particular fact, the initial burden is on him to prove the same.
In the present case, claimants contended that the deceased was working as Lab Assistant in Soil Science Department, GKVK.
The burden of proving that fact was on the claimants.
In the first round of NC: 2023:KHC:21285-DB litigation, the claimants have not adduced any evidence in that regard.
On their request, the matter was remanded.

In the course of the said order, this Court specifically observed that to prove his said employment and income from his employment, the claimants have neither produced the salary certificate nor examined the employer.
Despite such observation, after the remand though the claimants produced the salary details at Ex.P18, did not choose to examine the author of the said document.
14. It was contended that the said salary certificate was not disputed in the cross-examination of PW.1.
The respondent in the cross examination of PW.1 denied the employment of the deceased itself with GKVK.
Despite that Ex.P18 was not proved by examining the author of the same.
Under such circumstance, the Tribunal was not justified in holding that Ex.P18, consequently the employment of the deceased in GKVK and income of Rs.6,000/-per month by way of salary was proved.

Ex. P8 to 10, the degree certificate, computer course certificate and NSS Certificate were all of no help to show that the deceased had such employment or his income from GKVK or he being a JCB Supervisor.
NC: 2023:KHC:21285-DB 15.
It is material to note that the deceased, according to the claimants was BA Graduate.

Though claimants contend that he was working as Lab Assistant in Soil Science Dept., GKVK, he has not produced his appointment letter or proof of his eligibility in Geology or automobiles to operate JCB.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to accept his employment in GKVK or under PW. 2.

Thus,
income has to be notionally assessed.

The Managing Director vs Smt Anjenamma on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54398167/
4 16.
Having regard to the qualification, age of the deceased, prevailing wage rates and cost of living during 2012, his income can be notionally assessed at Rs.7,000/-.per month.
As per judgment in National Insurance co.Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others1 as the deceased had no permanent employment, 40% has to be super-added to his income by way of future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance co.Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore,
monthly income of the deceased comes to (Rs.7000 + 2800) Rs.9800/-.
Since deceased was bachelor 50% of his income has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Therefore, the monthly contribution to the family comes to Rs.4,900/-.
Multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is '17'.

Thus, the 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) NC: 2023:KHC:21285-DB compensation payable towards `loss of dependency' would be Rs.9,99,600/- (Rs.4,900 x 12 x 17).
17.
The claimants are the aged parents and unmarried sisters of the deceased.

Therefore, as per the judgments in Pranay Sethi's case referred to supra and Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., vs.
Nanu Ram alias Charu Ram and others2, they are entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- each with escalation at 10%.

entities.text:
Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., vs.
Nanu Ram alias Charu Ram and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case they are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on the head of loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses with escalation at 10%.
Therefore, the just compensation payable is as follows:
Sl . Heads

Amount in  No. Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 9,99,600/-
 2. Loss of consortium 2,20,000/-
 3. Towards Funeral and 33,000/-
 loss of Estate
18. Since Ex.P18 is not accepted by this Court, the additional evidence sought to be produced under I.A.3/17 is (2017) 16 SCC 680 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:21285-DB redundant.
Therefore, said application is liable to be dismissed.
19. For the aforesaid reasons, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is partly allowed.
IA No.3/2017 is dismissed.

(ii) The award in MVC No.5846/2012 is modified as follows:
(a) The claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.12,52,600/- with interest at 6%
from the date of petition till realization.
b) The appellant shall deposit the said amount on adjusting the amount already The Managing Director vs Smt Anjenamma on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54398167/
5 deposited, if any, before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
(c) On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall release the same to the claimants digitally on furnishing relevant documents.
(d) The order of the Tribunal with regard to apportionment is maintained.
